column1: # Mutation-testing baselines — a RATCHET, not a to-do list, and NOT a claim that the
# remaining survivors are harmless.
# SPANS IS AT ITS FLOOR — 10, and all ten are EQUIVALENT MUTANTS (measured 2026-08-13).
# Do not spend another pass on `spans`. Tests were written for all ten, the file was
# registered in MODULE_TESTS[spans], coverage reached 98%, and the count did not move —
# because none of the ten can change observable behaviour:
#   * a corrupted `style` default or fallback is normalised back, and `_placeholder`
#     falls through to the label form for ANY unrecognised value (incl. None);
#   * `not text or not spans` -> `and` reaches the same answer via `if not applied`;
#   * `char_start > cursor` -> `>=` and `cursor < n` -> `<=` append the empty string;
#   * both `build_word_offsets` mutants sit on the FIRST `idx < 0` guard, where the
#     fallback `text.find(token)` re-finds the same index.
# Full reasoning: backend/tests/redaction/test_apply_redactions_mutants.py.
# Lowering this baseline requires changing spans.py, not adding tests.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# "Kill every surviving mutant" is not a finishable goal on this codebase: an AST census of
# lockout's 149 survivors (regenerate mutmut's mutants from the source, map each survivor back
# to the line it edits, ask whether that line is inside a logging call) finds 58 that edit a log
# string and 8 that flip a condition guarding only a log call. No caller can observe those, and
# asserting on log text creates tests that break on every reword. Without a bounded definition
# of done, each pass closes a few real gaps and leaves a large residue — which reads as no
# progress.
# So the gate is: the survivor count for a module may go DOWN, never UP. A new untested
# predicate raises it and fails `--check-baseline`. That is the same shape as the coverage
# `fail_under` ratchet in backend/pyproject.toml, and for the same reason.
# READ THE NUMBERS AS A CEILING, NOT AS AN ALL-CLEAR. The same census over all six modules puts
# 167 of the 636 survivors (26%) in the log-string / log-branch bucket. The other 461 are
# ordinary predicates, comparisons, assignments and default arguments — code a caller CAN
# observe, and each one is a line the suite executes without checking. The counts below bound
# the residue; they do not excuse it.
# This file is READ by `./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --check-baseline`. It is not
# documentation: a checked-in table nothing reads goes stale, which is exactly how
# `expected-schemas.tsv` died. It went stale here anyway — two of the notes below described
# measurements nobody had made (see spans and lockout) — so every note now states what was
# measured and how.
# ⚠️ ALL SIX ROWS CURRENTLY AWAIT RE-MEASUREMENT. `--check-baseline` reports them NOT MEASURED
# (exit 4), because a run log is only admissible with the completion + source-binding evidence
# a run now writes beside it (<key>.meta), and the 2026-08-12 logs predate that. The numbers
# below are the last recorded LEVEL, not a verified state. Two of them are independently known
# to be stale: regenerating mutants from today's source produces 10 mutants security.log names
# but the current app/core/security.py cannot make (c0c462aa changed it), and security's own
# note already said its verify_token gap closed after the run.
# HOW TO UPDATE
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --clean            # stale cached verdicts are the #1 trap
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --module <name>
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --check-baseline <name>
# Lower the number when you have added tests. NEVER raise it to make a run pass — that is the
# one move this file exists to prevent. Raising it needs a reason in the commit message.
# COVERAGE is recorded alongside because a survivor count is meaningless without it: a module
# whose selected tests execute 56% of it reports survivors that measure test SELECTION, not
# test strength. That happened to `lockout` and produced 41 false findings in `dependencies`.
# module<TAB>max_survivors<TAB>min_coverage_pct<TAB>measured_on<TAB>note

column5: 10 survivors of 206, and ALL TEN ARE EQUIVALENT (verified 2026-08-13 by writing tests for every one: registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage 97%->98%, count unmoved). Corrects the previous note, which called 5 of them 'operator flips in live predicates' — those 5 are equivalent too: `or`->`and` reaches the same answer via `if not applied`; `char_start > cursor`->`>=` and `cursor < n`->`<=` append the empty string; and BOTH `idx < 0` mutants sit on the FIRST guard, where the fallback `text.find(token)` re-finds the same index. This is a FLOOR: lowering it needs a change to spans.py, not more tests. Reasoning: tests/redaction/test_apply_redactions_mutants.py.

column1: lockout
column5: 149 -> 72 (measured, not predicted -- the previous note's "83 real gaps" was a census guess and was off by 6). Every one of the 149 was read and classified: 77 real, all killed by tests/unit/test_lockout_survivor_mutants.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage 85% -> 86%); 70 noise (log strings, or a condition guarding only a `logger.info`/`logger.warning` call -- `_apply_successful_login`'s and `_check_and_record_attempt_memory`'s `failed_attempts > 0 or locked_until_dt` gate nothing but the log, the resets below run unconditionally either way); 2 equivalent. First equivalence proof: `_cas_write`'s `expected or ""` -> `expected or "XXXX"` -- `_decode_stored` only ever returns `None` or a non-empty string, so `expected` is never a falsy-non-None value and the mutated fallback is unreachable. Second, found by MEASURING rather than trusting a diff (149->77 predicted, 149->72 actual): `_check_and_record_attempt_memory`'s expiry-reset `record.first_failed_attempt = now.isoformat()` -> `None` is masked because the SAME call's success/failure branch (an exhaustive if/else on `success`, always taken immediately after) unconditionally re-stamps the field with the identical `now` regardless of the mutation -- the success branch sets it to `None` outright and the failure branch's own `is None` guard re-fires. Two near-duplicate code paths (Redis-backed, in-memory-fallback) each got their own tests; a mutant's diff can look like it belongs to the wrong one. Full reasoning: tests/unit/test_lockout_survivor_mutants.py.

column1: security
column5: 95 -> 19 (measured twice: a first pass predicted 82 real/13 equivalent from the diffs alone and the re-measurement came back at 19 survivors, not 13 — six `_create_password_context` scheme-name-casing mutants (`mutmut_15/17/19/40/42/44`, e.g. `schemes=["pbkdf2_sha256",...]` -> `["PBKDF2_SHA256",...]`) were wrongly predicted real; passlib's `CryptContext` resolves scheme names case-insensitively, confirmed by direct interpreter experiment, so they construct a byte-identical context and were reclassified equivalent). Final: 76 real, all killed by tests/unit/test_security_survivor_mutants.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage 79% -> 92%) — five families: `_create_password_context`'s exact CryptContext schemes/default/deprecated/rounds kwargs (29 of 37, the other 8 equivalent — see below), `needs_rehash_for_fips_v3`'s own parsing/threshold logic (20 of 20 — unreachable through the real `pwd_context.needs_update()` for most inputs since passlib already flags any rounds mismatch, so isolated with a stub `pwd_context`), `authenticate_user`'s `allow_local_fallback` argument actually reaching `local_password_allowed` (5 of 8), `create_access_token`'s `jti` uniqueness and `expires_delta` arithmetic (3 of 4), and `verify_token`'s response-body/audit-record exact shape (19 of 24 — two HTTPException sites share identical detail/headers literals and each site's untested half survived; the FIPS legacy-algorithm-fallback audit call's event_type/outcome/dict keys were asserted for only one field). 19 equivalent, all verified by reading the exact code path or (passlib-specific) by direct interpreter experiment: 8 in `_create_password_context` (2 `default=` kwarg dropped, falling back to the first `schemes=` entry which already matches; 6 the case-insensitive scheme-name mutants above), 5 in `verify_token` + 1 in `accepted_algorithms` + 1 in `create_access_token` all collapsing to the same already-proven fact that `signing_algorithm`/`accepted_algorithms` discard their `token_type` argument, 1 in `_bcrypt_rounds` (a non-"true"-yielding string default is indistinguishable from the real ""), 3 in `authenticate_user` (getattr default on a non-nullable mapped column is dead code, same proof class as `dependencies`'s 18). No production bug found — every real gap was existing correct behaviour that lacked an assertion. Full reasoning: tests/unit/test_security_survivor_mutants.py.

column1: session
column5: 73 -> 46 (measured twice, identical both times: 226 mutants, coverage 76% -> 82%). The stale note's "40 other" was a census guess, not measured -- re-read from a fresh run per the handoff rather than trusted. Every one of the 73 was read and classified: 27 real, all killed by tests/unit/test_session_survivor_mutants.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage 76% -> 82%) -- five families: `_get_store`'s cold-boot/reprobe-crash edges (the `_store_initialized` guard inverted makes the whole first-call branch permanently unreachable, landing every call on the reprobe-gated `elif` instead; `_last_redis_probe = now` -> `None` crashes the call AFTER NEXT with `now - None`; the bottom-of-function `_in_memory_store` safety net returning bare `None` after a later outage), `_record_degradation`'s `.labels(control=, fallback=)` kwargs actually reaching the metric (nothing called the real function -- every existing caller mocks `_record_degradation` itself), `InMemoryStore`'s expiry boundary (`>`/`<=` at the exact instant) and prefix isolation (`and`->`or` leaks a foreign-namespace or already-expired key; `rstrip("*")`->`rstrip("XX*XX")` over-strips a prefix ending in `X`) and TTL propagation (`set`'s `expire_at = None` makes an explicitly-TTL'd value immortal), `OIDCStateStore.__init__`'s falsy-not-None sentinel (`self._store = ""` breaks `is None` lazy-load, permanently skipping `_get_store()`), and `_count_states`/`_scan_keys`'s SCAN `match=` pattern actually reaching Redis (dropped/nulled scans the WHOLE keyspace shared with `lockout` and the Celery broker -- false exhaustion refusals off foreign key volume, or cleanup deleting a lockout counter / Celery result key) plus `_scan_keys` collecting the real key not `None` (a nulled collection makes exhaustion-cap cleanup a permanent no-op), and `store_state`'s documented 600s default, its `_cleanup_oldest_states(100)` call (dropped to `None` crashes `_scan_keys`'s `len(collected) >= limit` the instant Redis's cleanup path runs under real load), its post-cleanup cap boundary (`>=`->`>` is an off-by-one bypass) paired with the SAME branch's `return False`->`True` (reports success while never calling `store.set()`, handing the login flow an unredeemable state), and its own `ex=expires_seconds` reaching the backing store. 13 equivalent, verified by reading the exact code path (three by direct interpreter experiment): `_get_store`'s first-site `_in_memory_store=None` (already proven+documented in test_auth_state_degradation.py -- the function's OWN second, bottom site unconditionally re-creates it); three `datetime.now(UTC)`->`datetime.now(None)` mutants (naive `.timestamp()` assumes local time and produces the identical POSIX epoch second, confirmed by direct experiment: 1.6e-05s apart, not a systematic offset); `InMemoryStore.delete`'s `return 1`->`return 2` (every one of the three call sites in `app/` reads the return value only as a truthiness check -- grepped); `InMemoryStore.set`'s no-TTL `expire_at = None`->`""` (both read sites use plain truthiness, `is None` never appears); four Redis `count=500` mutants across `_count_states`/`_scan_keys` (redis-py's own `scan_iter` signature default for `count` is already `None`, confirmed via `inspect.signature` -- COUNT is a per-round-trip batch-size hint that never changes the final result set); `_cleanup_oldest_states`'s unreachable default (`count: int = 100`->`101` -- the sole production caller and every existing test always pass an explicit value). 33 noise (log strings, or a condition/argument feeding only a log call). Two real gaps worth flagging as operationally significant even though the code as WRITTEN was already correct: the SCAN `match=` cross-subsystem leak, and `store_state`'s `return True` on a state that was never stored. No production bug required a fix -- every real gap was existing, correct behaviour lacking an assertion. Full reasoning: tests/unit/test_session_survivor_mutants.py.

column1: dependencies
column5: 175 -> 79 (measured three times before trusted: two intermediate runs raced a concurrent agent's pre-commit stash/restore against an uncommitted MODULE_TESTS edit and had to be discarded as NOT stale_cache=0). Every one of the 175 read and classified: 96 real, all killed by tests/unit/test_dependencies_survivor_mutants.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage steady at 94%) — dominated by two families: HTTPException response-body dict/headers exact-equality (existing suites checked `detail["code"]` or a truthy message, never the exact string/key/headers, so a reworded message or a renamed `"message"` key survived) and predicates/boundaries/dropped-arguments with real consequences (banner-ack tzinfo normalization + its `>=`/`>` boundary, account-expiry `<`/`<=` boundary, the JWT `algorithms=` allowlist actually reaching `jwt.decode`, the httpOnly-cookie fallback, `request.state.user_id`/`org_id` stamping, `_enforce_approval`'s `db` argument reaching `approval_required` rather than a process-cache fallback, `verify_external_token` receiving the real `request`, the TESTING-only mock user's fields, `_route_path`'s strip-charset/length boundary). 52 noise (log-only strings/branches, plus `_enforce_proxy_identity_consistency`'s `revoke_all_sessions(reason=...)` — confirmed by reading the callee that `reason` only ever reaches its own log calls). 27 equivalent, MEASURED not guessed: 3 mutants (`_banner_requirement`'s `or`->`and`, and both `accepted_algorithms(None)` siblings) were first written up as real, given tests, and reported SURVIVED on `--verify` — each then got a written equivalence proof rather than a second guess (`_banner_requirement`: `hasattr(None,"query")` is already False so the `or`'s first disjunct is a strict subset of the second, and the enclosing `try/except` closes the remaining gap; `accepted_algorithms(None)`: `core.security.signing_algorithm` discards its argument). The other 24: 18 `getattr(user/external_user, "<mapped column>", DEFAULT)` mutants where only DEFAULT changed — every caller in this module is a genuine SQLAlchemy `User` ORM instance (verified empirically: an unset mapped column returns `None`, never raises), so the default is dead code; `_route_path`'s inner default neutralised by its own outer `or ""`; 3 case-only `TESTING` env-fallback variants neutralised by `.lower()`; 2 `TokenPayload(jti=...)` mutants whose field is constructed and never read. No production bug found — every real gap was existing correct behaviour that lacked an assertion. Full reasoning: tests/unit/test_dependencies_survivor_mutants.py. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-28 from scratch (previous logs predated the completion+source-binding evidence this file's header describes, so they were NOT MEASURED under `--check-baseline` and could not be trusted): 793 mutants, 83 survived — a 4-mutant REGRESSION over this row's `79`, traced to a single intervening commit (1b536070) that added `"trigger": "fixed_date"` to `_enforce_account_expiry`'s audit `details` (making the module docstring's "AUTH_ACCOUNT_EXPIRED distinguished by details.trigger" claim true — `account_lifecycle_service.py`'s inactivity sweep already emitted `trigger="inactivity"`) with no accompanying test. All 4 (`x__enforce_account_expiry__mutmut_27/28/29/30`, the key and value each mutated two ways) confirmed REAL via `--verify`, fixed by one new test asserting the exact `details` dict (`TestEnforceAccountExpiry::test_the_audit_details_are_tagged_with_the_fixed_date_trigger`), re-verified KILLED. The other 78 survivors were confirmed byte-identical to the prior triage (git diff of the module between the two measurements touches only the 4-line `details=` literal, so every other function's mutants are unchanged; spot-checked two — `_enforce_proxy_identity_consistency`'s `mutmut_12`/`mutmut_33` — against `--show` and both match the documented getattr-DEFAULT and `revoke_all_sessions(reason=)` classes). Count returns to 79 after the fix; this row's `79`/`93` need no change.

column1: password_policy
column5: 86 -> 46 of 292, and 46 is a FLOOR unless password_policy.py itself changes: every one of the 46 was classified from its diff and the classification then MEASURED. 40 killed by the new tests/unit/test_password_policy_mutants.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage 94% -> 100%), and the 46 left are EXACTLY the 43 noise + 3 equivalent predicted before the run, id for id. The 43 noise all sit in check_password_history's degradation report — the logger.warning/logger.exception strings, the 7 fragments of the operator %s message, and the checked/unverifiable counters, which feed only that message's %d slots (the critical-vs-error LEVEL split, which is what an alert keys off, is already pinned by test_password_policy_controls.py). The 3 equivalent: the wrapper's new_password_hash="" -> None/"XXXX" (the method never reads that parameter) and history_count <= 0 -> < 0 (the two disagree only at 0, where the mutant falls through to password_history[:0], an empty slice, and returns True anyway). The 40 kills were each control-verified BEFORE the run by monkeypatching the individual mutant function from the gitignored mutants/ copy and watching a test fail — with the unmutated __mutmut_orig, the 3 equivalents and 3 noise mutants as negative controls, all of which correctly reported SURVIVED (the first version of that harness reported KILLED for everything, including orig, because a stray /tmp/token.py shadowed the stdlib). Biggest real gaps closed: the module-level wrappers (get_days_until_expiration/is_password_expired/password_expiry_cutoff) were never called with an explicit current_time, so dropping the caller's clock and answering "as of now" was invisible; is_password_expired's <= cutoff boundary and its return True for a NULL password_changed_at; every tzinfo normalisation in expiry_cutoff/is_password_expired/get_days_until_expiration (3 mutants each, all killed at once by a naive input, which raises TypeError); max_age_days <= 0 -> <= 1 and history_count <= 0 -> <= 1, each turning the smallest configurable nonzero value into a second off switch; and the uppercase/lowercase/digit error strings, which are response-body text the SPA renders, not log output.
